column3: Close to the Hebrew; “Noisy” is rendered “a brawler,” and “staggers” as “is intoxicated.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Missing his life” is rendered “forfeits his own life.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Cessation from strife” is rendered “Keeping away from strife,” and “bursts out” as “will quarrel.”
Close to the Hebrew; “From winter” is rendered “after the autumn,” and NASB adds “So.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB adds “like” (“like deep water”).
Close to the Hebrew; “A multitude of persons” is rendered “Many a man,” and “a person of faithfulness” as “a trustworthy man.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew; “Winnowing” is rendered “Disperses.”

Close to the Hebrew; “A weight and a weight, a measure and a measure” is rendered “Differing weights and differing measures.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Makes himself known” is rendered “distinguishes himself,” and “a youth” as “a lad.”

Close to the Hebrew; “Lest you become impoverished” is rendered “or you will become poor.”

Close to the Hebrew; “An article of preciousness” is rendered “a more precious thing.”
The gloss follows the reading tradition (Qere) “a foreign woman”; NASB’s plural “foreigners” reflects the written text (Kethiv).
Close to the Hebrew; “Food of falsehood” is rendered “Bread obtained by falsehood.”
“Plans are established by counsel” is rendered as a command, “Prepare plans by consultation.”
Close to the Hebrew; “One who opens his lips” is rendered “a gossip,” and NASB adds “Therefore.”
Close to the Hebrew; “And his mother” is rendered “or his mother.”

Close to the Hebrew; “A weight and a weight” is rendered “Differing weights,” and “balances of deceit” as “a false scale.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Are from Yahweh” is rendered “are ordained by the LORD.”
Close to the Hebrew; “To consider” is rendered “to make inquiry.”
Close to the Hebrew; “He brought back over them a wheel” is rendered “drives the threshing wheel over them.”
Close to the Hebrew; “The breath of a human” is rendered “The spirit of man,” and “the chambers of the belly” as “the innermost parts of his being.”
The Hebrew repeats “loyalty” in the second line; NASB has “by righteousness.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Wounds of bruises [are] a cleansing in evil” is rendered “Stripes that wound scour away evil,” and NASB adds “reach.” The meaning is uncertain.
